subject: Private Control Plane: AuthZ delegation model & SAML/SCIM decision log
messages:
From: Judy Liu <judy.liu@streamexample.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: idp-team@streamexample.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private CP access model: SAML attributes & SCIM group mapping (initial req)

Rishi / Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. We're running into two blockers as we prep for our VPC/private control plane deployment:

- Our IdP sends nested groups and uses "employeeType" and "roleTitle" attributes. We need guidance on which attributes Redwood expects for operator/admin assignment.
- We want SCIM-driven provisioning for team accounts but keep a separate path for service accounts and automated jobs. How best to map SCIM groups to Redwood IAM roles?

Attached is a short requirements doc from our security team. High level asks: strict least-privilege by default, clear break-glass, and auditability to satisfy our compliance team.

Can you propose a binding model and optional fallback for air-gapped operator onboarding? Also please call out any gaps in our IdP schema.

Judy
Judy Liu
Director, Identity & Security
StreamExample, Inc.

Attachment: streamexample-privcp-requirements.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Judy Liu <judy.liu@streamexample.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP access model: SAML attributes & SCIM group mapping (initial req)

Judy / Naomi / Laura,

Thanks Judy. Quick read-through below and a proposed model for your team to review. TL;DR: we recommend SCIM group -> role binding + SAML attribute assertions as the canonical source of truth for session elevation.

Proposal (high level):
- SCIM group mapping: provision SCIM groups for "redwood:team:<team-name>" and map to base roles: Viewer, Operator, Admin, Audit. SCIM members become base-role holders.
- SAML assertions for elevation: use a short-lived SAML assertion attribute "redwood:session_role" that can be present for elevated actions (canary deploys, schema changes). Redwood will validate assertion TTL and issuer.
- Service accounts: register as "service_account" object via SCIM with explicit owner team metadata and no UI login. Service accounts get scoped service roles (e.g., inference-runner, metrics-writer).
- Break-glass: maintain an emergency admin list managed outside SCIM (signed ticket + ephemeral certs) for air-gapped recovery.
- Audit: emit role-change events to your syslog/Kafka + include SAML assertion metadata in every elevated session log.

Open questions for IdP team:
1) Do you currently normalize nested groups or pass membership flattened?
2) Can you emit custom attributes like "redwood:session_role" with a 10m TTL?

I'll attach a short decision diagram and an updated authz model for discussion. If agreed, we can lock this as the canonical mapping and draft the SCIM schema annotations.

Next step: 30-min sync to walk the model and confirm IdP capabilities. Proposed slots: Mon 9/20 10–10:30 PT or Tue 9/21 14–14:30 PT.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Judy Liu <judy.liu@streamexample.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP access model: SAML attributes & SCIM group mapping (notes)

Adding a few operational considerations I want in the decision log:

- Canary / Rollout: when we enable elevation for a team, we should gate by IP allowlist + enforcement window (e.g., 9am–6pm) for the first 48h.
- Role churn: implement a 24h caching TTL for SCIM group-to-role resolution to avoid auth storms during large directory syncs.
- Delegation pattern: allow team-level delegation (team-admins) for non-security actions, but require at least one cross-team Admin to approve production-impact changes.
- SCIM schema: include a "redwood:owner_contact" field on group metadata (email) so we can automate rollout notifications.

I'll attach the updated model (authz-model-v2.pdf) and a spreadsheet with proposed SCIM attributes. Dev, can you confirm service-account onboarding flow?

-naomi

Attachment: authz-model-v2.pdf; scim-schema-annotations.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP access model: SAML attributes & SCIM group mapping (service account detail)

Quick follow-ups from infra: 

- Service accounts will be provisioned with a unique key ID and a binding to a team SCIM group. We need to decide whether keys rotate via the customer's KMS or our managed rotation. Recommend: default to customer KMS for Private deployments; fall back to managed rotation for Dedicated.
- Break-glass technical: implement a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) gateway that accepts a CA-signed ticket for emergency elevation; record issuance in audit log with issuer fingerprint.
- Role chaining: we will support a single-step elevation (base role -> session_role). Multiple chained elevations are harder to reason about in audits and we should avoid unless there's a clear need.

Laura, can you review the compliance acceptance criteria so we can converge on the audit payload fields?

-Dev
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Judy Liu <judy.liu@streamexample.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Decision: AuthZ delegation model for Private Control Plane (final)

Folks — thanks for the input. This thread captures the decision and next steps. Please treat this as the canonical decision log for the StreamExample proof-of-concept.

Decision summary (approved):
- Canonical identity sources: SCIM groups = base role assignment; SAML assertion ("redwood:session_role") = ephemeral elevation for privileged actions.
- Service accounts: provision via SCIM as type=service_account. Keys prefer customer KMS in Private installs; fallback to Redwood-managed rotation only if customer KMS unavailable.
- Break-glass: signed ticket -> JWT gateway; emergency admins listed in a separate break-glass ACL (not SCIM).
- Operational controls: 24h SCIM caching TTL; IP gating + 48h rollout window for initial elevation enablement; session logs must include SAML assertion metadata and group resolution snapshot.

Deliverables / owners:
- Rishi: finalize decision log and publish internal doc link (done).
- Naomi: produce rollout checklist and SCIM attribute spreadsheet (attachment).
- Dev: implement JWT gateway + KMS integration tests (ETA: 2027-10-14).
- Laura: verify audit payload schema meets compliance (ETA: 2027-10-07).

Attachments published: authz-model-v2.pdf, scim-schema-annotations.xlsx

If StreamExample's IdP can emit the proposed session_role attribute with a 10-minute TTL, we can start the SCIM mapping pilot next week. Judy — can your IdP team confirm by EOD Mon 10/4?

Thanks all,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
